scope: Fail-closed capability taxonomy from inspected GitHub, GitLab and Gerrit contracts; provider surface and phase are explicit

states.name: INTENT_HEAD_BOUND
states.meaning: The effect request is bound to an exact reviewed source/head or patch-set revision.

states.name: REQUEST_OPERATION_ID_BOUND
states.meaning: A server-assigned identifier exists early enough to recover an ambiguous request/admission without blindly reissuing the effect.

states.name: QUEUE_OR_TRAIN_ADMITTED
states.meaning: Server has admitted the change into asynchronous queue/train processing.

states.name: CI_STATE_BOUND
states.meaning: A pipeline/check execution is bound to the queue/train candidate state. Synthetic merge-group/train SHAs are not final target-ref SHAs.

states.name: FINAL_TARGET_REF_EFFECT_EXACT
states.meaning: The exact protected/target ref transition that actually landed is durably observed.

states.name: POST_EFFECT_GROUP_ID_BOUND
states.meaning: A server identifier groups the actual submitted effects after completion. This can aid attribution/revert/audit but cannot necessarily recover a pre-effect ambiguous request.

states.name: POST_EFFECT_POLICY_EXACT
states.meaning: Server-derived policy/submit evidence is exact-read and bound to the landed effect or submitted group, preserving bypass/override/evaluate-only semantics.

github.REQUEST_OPERATION_ID_BOUND: async merge UUID; 409 existing-UUID recovery requires pending expected_head_sha/merge_method/merge_action comparison
github.QUEUE_OR_TRAIN_ADMITTED: terminal async status enqueued; this is terminal only for the request, not the final merge
github.CI_STATE_BOUND: merge-group/check-run evidence; merge-group SHA is queue-group state
github.POST_EFFECT_GROUP_ID_BOUND: the same async UUID can identify terminal request result while retained, but the result endpoint expires after 24h and split stack groups require separate final-effect closure
github.POST_EFFECT_POLICY_EXACT: Rule Suite exact tuple/id readbacks; active result pass/bypass and evaluation_result separated

gitlab.INTENT_HEAD_BOUND: merge-train add sha or merge-request merge sha
gitlab.REQUEST_OPERATION_ID_BOUND: merge-train car/entry integer id returned/listed for the admitted MR
gitlab.CI_STATE_BOUND: train pipeline id/SHA/status; later cars can be canceled/recreated when earlier train membership changes
gitlab.FINAL_TARGET_REF_EFFECT_EXACT: merged MR attribution plus exact target-branch ref evidence; commit fields are merge-method-sensitive
gitlab.POST_EFFECT_GROUP_ID_BOUND: the same car id is visible in complete-scope train entries with merged status/merged_at in the inspected contract
gitlab.POST_EFFECT_POLICY_EXACT: train pipeline outcome plus merged MR state; no GitHub-Rule-Suite-equivalent per-ref policy object is claimed

gerrit.INTENT_HEAD_BOUND: POST /changes/{change-id}/revisions/{revision-id}/submit addresses one exact patch-set revision
gerrit.REQUEST_OPERATION_ID_BOUND: NOT_OBSERVED in the inspected submit contract: submit returns ChangeInfo, but submission_id is documented only for status MERGED, so it is not assumed to exist before effect completion
gerrit.QUEUE_OR_TRAIN_ADMITTED: not modeled as a merge queue in the inspected Gerrit submit contract
gerrit.CI_STATE_BOUND: submit requirements/plugin submit rules are current server policy evidence; pre-submit snapshots are not replayable effect leases
gerrit.FINAL_TARGET_REF_EFFECT_EXACT: read the destination ref after submit because submit type may merge, fast-forward, rebase or cherry-pick and can create a commit different from the reviewed patch set
gerrit.POST_EFFECT_GROUP_ID_BOUND: ChangeInfo.submission_id is set for MERGED changes, shared by changes in one submission, and should be captured with Submitted Together closure; its string format is explicitly not a contract
gerrit.POST_EFFECT_POLICY_EXACT: MERGED ChangeInfo + submission_id + preserved submit-requirement/override evidence; historical ChangeInfo can be read at a NoteDb meta SHA

recovery_consequences: GitHub and GitLab expose request/admission IDs early enough to be recovery anchors after ambiguous asynchronous admission; Gerrit's inspected revision-submit API instead offers an exact patch-set path and a post-effect submission group ID, not an observed pre-effect request ID.
A post-effect submission/group ID must not be retroactively treated as proof that an ambiguous request was uniquely admitted before final state is observed.

If an effect response is ambiguous and no request-operation ID exists, recover by reading exact resource state first; only retry when that read proves the intended effect has not occurred and the effect endpoint's idempotency/precondition semantics make retry safe.

Group closure is a separate authority axis: GitHub stack member vector, GitLab train car membership, and Gerrit Submitted Together closure all need durable capture where one trigger may affect multiple changes.
cross_provider_invariants: Pre-effect authorization/policy reads are not leases unless the effect API atomically consumes that exact authorization revision.
Expected-head/revision binding, request-operation identity, group closure, final target-ref effect and post-effect policy evidence are independent axes.
Queue/train admission and CI success are not final target-ref effect.
Final effect is proven against the target repository ref, not a synthetic merge-group/train pipeline SHA.
Bypass, override and evaluate-only outcomes remain distinct from enforced pass.
Ambiguous mutation responses are recovered by exact state/operation readback before retry.
